tldr: The Chain-of-Ideas (CoI) agent organizes relevant literature in a chain structure mirroring progressive research development, enabling LLMs to generate novel, human-comparable research ideas and experimental designs at low cost.
contributions: Propose the CoI agent framework that organizes literature in a chain structure to mirror progressive research development, improving LLM ideation capabilities
Propose Idea Arena, a pairwise evaluation protocol using Round-Robin tournament ELO scoring that shows high agreement (70.8%) with human researchers
Demonstrate through extensive experiments that CoI agent consistently outperforms all automated baselines and generates ideas comparable to human experts
methods: The CoI agent operates in three stages: (1) CoI Construction — given a research topic, the LLM generates multiple perspective queries to retrieve anchor papers, then extends each chain backward (via references) and forward (via citing papers) using Semantic Scholar and embedding-based ranking, terminating at milestone papers or preset length; (2) Idea Generation — the LLM predicts future trends from each CoI, consolidates ideas step-by-step (motivation → impact → realization), and a novelty-checker agent iteratively refines drafts against existing literature; (3) Experiment Design — the LLM designs experiments using few-shot examples from existing papers, refined iteratively by a review agent. The best idea across branches is selected via pairwise comparison.
results: CoI agent consistently ranks first among all automated baselines in both model-based and human evaluations, surpassing the second-best methods (GPT-Researcher and RAG) by 108 and 56 ELO scores respectively. Performance is on par with the Real Paper baseline and excels in Novelty and Significance. Human-model agreement reaches 70.8% average. The agent costs a minimum of $0.50 to generate a candidate idea and its corresponding experimental design.
limitations: CoI agent still lags considerably behind Real Paper in Clarity, Feasibility, and Expected Effectiveness under human evaluation, attributed to the absence of extensive experimental validation for model-generated ideas. The paper also notes that a single CoI may be insufficient to capture the most promising direction, requiring multiple branches.
